Re-running a job left the previous attempt's artifact in place. Coverage then downloaded that older package by name and failed a passed UT, because the manifest still said the first attempt failed. Closes #301.

## What changes

`actions/upload-artifact@v4` keeps an existing artifact unless `overwrite` is true. On PR #295, run 38526631198, the failed UT uploaded `ut-coverage` (`status: FAIL`, 3821/3822). The re-run passed and uploaded a second package with the same name. Uploads that a later job downloads by exact name now replace the previous attempt:

- `ut-coverage`
- `st-coverage`
- `mocked-e2e-plan`
- `real-e2e-plan`

`.ci/ci-contract.test.mjs` fails if a workflow downloads an artifact by exact name and the matching upload omits `overwrite: true`.

- WSL, `node --test --test-name-pattern "latest attempt" .ci/ci-contract.test.mjs`: 1 passed, 0 failed.

303.body:
Chat Completions responses can contain zero-filled `input_tokens` / `output_tokens` compatibility fields alongside valid `prompt_tokens` / `completion_tokens`. The model client preferred those aliases, so a response reporting 30,393 prompt tokens and 84 completion tokens was persisted as zero output tokens.

Use one shared usage normalizer with the actual request protocol. Chat Completions prefers prompt/completion; Responses and Anthropic prefer input/output. Aliases are fallbacks, not additional tokens. Explicit counts, including zero and counts that disagree with the reported total, are preserved; reasoning tokens are never added again. Without protocol context, a complete pair matching the total wins, including legitimate zero values. Only when neither pair matches does zero-fill recovery prefer a positive alias. Conflicting aliases retain diagnostics; when both pairs match, input/output keeps its existing precedence.

API session naming, paper vision, and evolution accounting now share the same Chat rules. Incomplete paper usage remains unknown instead of fabricating zero counts. The adapter consumes normalized internal usage events, and the metering proxy already uses the correct Chat precedence; neither needs a rule change. E2E assertions and research-delivery behavior are unchanged.

Tested commit: `3f06f6ed76c0d6d4e97e08ef2709a1e82b1d7fa8`, based on `bb356a3f474ee6382f05420b3cf05e24d60a756e`. The follow-up adds one commit to the existing branch and changes only the shared normalizer and its unit tests; protocol-aware call sites are unchanged.

- Seven new unknown-protocol regressions all fail on the previous implementation. The complete normalization matrix now passes 19/19, including the reported `10/0/10` case, zero inputs, zero totals, matching-pair ties, and conflict diagnostics. Existing fallback tests also cover missing and inconsistent totals.
- Model typecheck: passed; the full UT layer's typecheck also passed.
- `pnpm ci:ut`: planned 3,833 / executed 3,833 / passed 3,833, 0 failed or skipped, JiuwenSwarm backend.
- `pnpm ci:st`: planned 3 / executed 3 / passed 3; SDK contract sub-suite: 66 passed plus 3 subtests.
- `pnpm ci:e2e`: planned 74 / executed 74 / passed 74, 0 failed or skipped; 9 additional JiuwenSwarm checks passed.
- Unmodified base `bb356a3f`: full UT planned 3,808 / executed 3,808 / passed 3,808, 0 failed or skipped, with a separate Swarm port group.

Earlier attempts encountered a dependency-download TLS failure, an incorrectly exported test dependency variable, and a parallel Swarm startup port collision. The final full UT runs used the standard environment and verified distinct bound ports. An intermediate blocked-queue assertion did not reproduce in the clean candidate or base runs. No assertion or product behavior was changed to resolve these validation issues.

## E2E user journeys

PASS at the current head — `pnpm ci:e2e` ran all 74 mocked browser journeys (research 20, standard 48, literature 6), plus the 9 Swarm checks above.

Historical targeted API evidence, tested at the first commit `c85c3cf8874a7571b47ea66e17d71209916efba1`: isolated production API and Runner CLIs with a local provider stub, using both native and JiuwenSwarm executors. Five scenarios per backend each completed a reply, queried persisted public `/usage`, and continued the same session: 20 completed Runs. Observed input/output/total tuples were `30393/84/30477`, `10/7/19`, `10/0/10`, and `8/5/13` for Responses and Anthropic; repeated cumulative frames did not increase totals. These targeted API journeys were not rerun for the unknown-protocol-only follow-up; the production callers explicitly pass their protocol and are unchanged.

The paid real-provider L3 suite was not rerun. E2E assertions and research-delivery behavior are unchanged.

311.body:
## What does this PR do / why do we need it

Implements the **full three-layer plan** for natural-language program evolution (GitHub issue #310): turn `/evolve-design` from a hidden slash command into something a natural-language sentence can trigger, with the framework actively recommending a tree-search evolution and the interaction staying natural-language end to end.

Today `/evolve-design` is a hidden slash command: a user must already know the prefix to start an evolution search, and the only visible entry is a button in the artifact detail modal that fills the composer with `/evolve-design make the artifact X better: ` (still requiring manual completion). The interaction is command-shaped, not natural-language.

### Layer 1 — Composer intent recognition (frontend)

- **`apps/web/src/evolve/intent.ts`** (new): pure `detectEvolveIntent(message)` — true only when an improvement verb pairs with an evolvable target (`program` / `code` / `algorithm` / `function` / `model` / `script` / `artifact` …). Non-evolvable targets (`formatting` / `layout` / `description` / `explanation`) never match, and bare "better" with no target never matches. `isEvolveDesignCommand()` separates the explicit slash command from natural language.
- **`EvolveSuggestionBar`** (new): a low-intrusion confirmation bar. Detection only *offers*; the user must explicitly accept before the algorithm picker opens — an evolution search spends real budget (mutations + sandboxed evaluations), so a false positive is worse than a missed suggestion.
- **`App.tsx`**: an explicit `/evolve-design` command opens the algorithm picker directly (existing behavior preserved); a natural-language intent shows the confirmation bar first, and only an accepted suggestion opens the picker. Both flags reset when the message leaves evolve intent.

### Layer 2 — Agent-driven recommendation (backend)

- **`packages/evolve/src/index.ts`**: the `create_evolve_run` tool description now tells the agent to **recommend** an evolution search when the user asks in natural language to improve a program / code / algorithm / model / result against a measurable target — not only when they type `/evolve-design`. The agent phrases it as a plain suggestion ("this looks like a search-shaped problem; want me to run an automated search that keeps the best-scoring variant?") and starts only after the user confirms. This builds on the evolve-design skill, whose description already lists natural-language triggers.

### Layer 3 — Visible entry points (frontend)

- **Composer**: a new sparkle "program evolution" button fills a natural-language prompt (`Improve the program: ` / `改进一下这个程序：`) instead of a slash command; `detectEvolveIntent` recognises it and offers the suggestion bar.
- **Artifact detail modal**: the evolve button now fills a natural-language seed prompt (`Make the artifact X better: ` / `让产物 X 变得更好：`) instead of the `/evolve-design ...` command text.
- **`intent.ts`**: adds `artifact` / `产物` as evolvable targets and `变得更好` as an improvement verb so both seed prompts are recognised.

### Why confirmation before the picker?

A search spends real budget. Detection is a guess, so it must only offer; the user's explicit accept is the gate. This is the core false-positive guard — a user saying "优化一下" while discussing formatting is never routed into an expensive search.

### Why verb+target pairing?

Intent detection is deliberately narrow: `优化一下界面布局` / `improve workflow steps` / `这个更好` / `make this better` all stay silent; only sentences pointing at an evolvable target (program / code / algorithm) match.

## Which issue(s) this PR fixes

Closes GitHub issue [#310](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/310).

## Test Plan and Test result

Verification commit: `f9fe5846` (9 files, +192/-5, single commit, based on GitHub main `cc974a14`)

- Web typecheck: `tsc --noEmit` passed, 0 errors
- Web unit tests: **107 passed / 0 failed** (includes 8 new evolve-intent tests)
- Web vite build: passed
- evolve package typecheck + tests: passed

Intent recognition behaviour verified:

| Input | Result |
|---|---|
| `improve the program` / `优化一下这个程序` / `让程序跑得更好` | triggers |
| `Make the artifact X better` / `让产物 X 变得更好` | triggers (seed prompts) |
| `make this better` / `这个更好` | no trigger (no explicit evolvable target) |
| `优化一下界面布局` / `improve workflow steps` / `改进一下说明文字` | no trigger (non-evolvable target) |
| `the first one is better` | no trigger (ordinary conversation) |
| explicit `/evolve-design` command | opens the picker directly, no confirmation bar (existing behavior preserved) |

## Self-checklist

- [x] **Design**: follows the issue's three-layer plan; confirmation-bar guard and narrow verb+target detection address false positives and budget protection
- [x] **Tests**: `evolve-intent.test.tsx` (8 tests) ships with this PR; typecheck and web unit tests pass
- [x] **Verification**: behaviour matrix recorded above with the verification commit
- [x] **Interface**: no public API change; reuses the existing `/api/evolve/runs` chain, `EvolveToolRuntime` and `EvolveAlgorithmPicker`
- [x] **Docs**: no website-doc change required for this frontend layer

# 学科知识引擎：摄取/生长/消解/消费全链 + 会话绑库与反幻觉运行时

> 与 GitCode MR [!125](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/merge_requests/125) 内容一致（对应 GitCode issue #86）。

把「学科知识」做成 SD 的一等资产：文献与结构化源摄取为带锚点溯源的知识图谱，图谱可离线生长、实体消解、社区聚类；对话内绑定知识库（kb scope）后，图谱成为受约束的知识来源，输出必须引用锚点，与证据账本 / 新颖性检查 / 引用核验构成多层反幻觉链路。

**283 文件，+50.8k，4 个按路径分组的 commit**（KE 核心 / agent 运行时 / Web / 技能与测试）。

---

## 新增功能

### 1. 知识引擎核心（`packages/knowledge-engine` + `services/api/src/knowledge-engine`）

- **存储域**：SQLite（知识库/文档/锚点/实体/边/社区/合并/作业/引用/公式），带迁移机制；算法核与存储分离，可独立评测
- **摄取**：LaTeX-first arXiv 通路（tar.gz 解包 + `\input` 递归内联）、JATS XML、视觉增强 PDF 解析；溯源门抽取——每个抽取结论挂文档锚点
- **生长**：离线 grow job，MMR + anchor-aware 多样本选择、收敛信号、结构化反思 directive 反哺下一轮
- **实体消解**：在线门 + 离线 job、物理合并与回滚（`ke_entity_merges`）、louvain 社区、根实体、社区报告
- **消费面**：`kb_search` / `kb_expand` / `doc_grep` 工具、entity_unified_search、三级文档阅读器（全文/结构/锚点）、引用 API（意图徽章 supporting / contrasting / mentioning + Similar / References / Cited-By）
- **REST**：`/api/ke/*` 全套 + 前端知识引擎页（cytoscape 图谱画布、生长控制面板、阅读器、引用面板）

### 2. 会话绑库（kb scope）

- session 设置新增 `kbScopeKbIds` / `kbScopeWebSearch` 运行时覆盖项；composer 底部选择器一键绑定/解绑，写路径为 fresh-GET 读改写，避免并发选择器互相回滚
- resident-summary 上下文贡献者持续注入**在库**图谱摘要（成熟度分级）；范围外知识库对工具面与摘要均不可见（防泄漏包装）
- 系统 prompt m8.3.1：上下文时钟、kb-scope 自管理指引、反编造纪律句——均在既有 5000 字符保护段预算内

### 3. 反幻觉与研究运行时

- 三级注入：证据账本（`evidence_ledger`）、新颖性检查（`novelty_check`）、引用核验（`verify_citation`）；KE 工具输出逐字文本打 nonce 不可信围栏
- finish-gate 收尾审计：技能声明 `metadata.pre-finish-audit` 即在收尾前注入审计 directive，有界续跑（≤2 次）
- 研究世界模型 `research_state`：目标钉住 / 计划生命周期 / 未决问题 / 已排除路径防复活 / 已试去重，JSON 文件锁崩溃可恢复
- 审批门计划生命周期（`packages/plan-mode`）：`propose_plan` / `revise_plan` 工具、约束级审批、版本绑定决策、决策日志；与上游 `update_plan` 快照机制共存（`AgentRunBindings` 同时携带 `planRepository` 与 `planStore`）
- stall-guard：模型调用无进展按空闲窗踢出重试（≤3 次），外层空闲看门狗兜底
- 记忆图谱镜像 `observeSessionPlan`；MCP 配置文件内容签名失效（保留上游按服务器签名比较，叠加文件级变更检测）

### 4. 技能包与评测

- 15 个方法论技能：knowledge-engine-explore/grow、evidence-notes、hypothesis-tournament、tree-search、robin-chain、virtual-lab、idea-debate、systematic-review、precise-qa、long-form-writing/audit、progressive-report、report-writer、table-analysis（多数声明 pre-finish-audit）
- 评测套件 `scripts/ke-*-eval.mjs`：growth delta-recall、discoverer 诚信维度、pairwise、citation（ALCE 三指标）、resolution、bench 539 题；`skill-test-runner` + ER 数据集构建器
- KE 旅程 E2E 9 条 + kb-scope / finish-gate 旅程，ke-stub 离线可跑

## 验证

Linux（Ubuntu WSL2），分支 `pr/knowledge-engine`（基于 upstream/main 最新 `ef65b6f`，4 个按路径分组的 commit）。

- 29 个 workspace 项目全量构建通过（含 web vite build）；`architecture:check` 通过（293 文件）
- 触及包测试全绿：workspace 119/119、context 50/50、tools 61/61、runtime-core 36/36、memory 35/35、schema 12/12、plan 5/5、plan-mode 2/2
- **services/api 全量套件 1020 tests / 1019 pass / 0 fail**（`node --test dist/*.test.js dist/**/*.test.js`，123s 干净退出）
- 与纯 upstream/main 对照树同环境跑 server.test.js 验证无回归：upstream 86/86，本分支 86/86；期间修复了三处合并引入的问题（MCP transport 双重 close、内置技能清单落位、保护段预算超限），并把 KE sqlite 连接补上服务器关闭回收（否则每个 boot 泄漏 db+wal+shm 句柄并在进程退出时挂起 drain）
- 双计划系统共存验证：propose_plan 审批门与 update_plan 快照在同 run 注册、互不干扰（context-assembly 集成测试覆盖）

Automatically generated Session titles could expose inline reasoning and were cut off at 24 characters even when that left an incomplete English phrase. This change generates complete summaries, filters reasoning, and separates stored titles from sidebar overflow styling.

## Changes

- Summarize the first message's core topic or intent in the user's language. Target 8–16 characters for CJK (maximum 24, including spaces and Latin names); target 3–6 words for other languages (maximum 8 whitespace-separated words and 80 Unicode characters).
- Regenerate once from the original message when the model exceeds the budget, returns an ellipsis, or reports truncated visible output. Preserve the complete accepted phrase instead of slicing it. Aggregate provider usage across successful responses.
- Use a neutral provisional `Session MM-DD HH:mm` title for long messages. Failed, empty, or still-invalid refinement retains that safe title; manual renames remain protected.
- Strip nested, unclosed and ordinary `<think>` blocks. Never use separate provider reasoning as the title.
- Keep sidebar ellipses in CSS; the existing full-title tooltip remains available. Existing stored titles and manual titles are not migrated.

## Policy and comparison evidence

The [title policy and acceptance examples](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/324cf7b2d0f3b2da4dc6ce7fe76674cfa3fb5346/docs/en/developer-docs/session-titles.md) document long Chinese/English cases and distinguish public evidence from assumptions. Open WebUI's public prompt and sidebar source show short topic summaries and CSS overflow; LibreChat documents a language-aware short-title prompt. Claude's help documents renaming but does not disclose its naming algorithm. The language budgets and bounded regeneration above are our own policy, not claimed competitor internals.

## Validation

Remote implementation: 324cf7b2d0f3b2da4dc6ce7fe76674cfa3fb5346. Its Git tree b8ee654a0d702a192673a8f1b7a26a7afb9d832b is verified identical to locally validated commit 1624420d544008eebc6f4c2cb856a7be85e6ff69. GitHub Git Data API was used because the Git transport was unreachable.

- Title unit suite: **16 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**. Cases include long Chinese/English outputs, regeneration, language-budget boundaries, incomplete output, nested reasoning, safe rejection and aggregated usage.
- Workspace build: **32 package/service projects completed**.
- API/schema type checks and `tsconfig.tests.json`: passed.
- Documentation: **127 files linted, 0 issues; 126 files checked for links**.
- E2E metadata: **62 spec files, 0 errors** (11 existing legacy warnings).
- Pinned Playwright discovery: **1 new journey discovered**.
- Local full UT/ST/mocked E2E layers could not complete on the available Windows host: Bash/process-spawning limitations prevent the Linux-oriented runners from reaching their cases. WSL provisioning was also unsuccessful. These are coverage limitations, not passing results. No real-model quality evaluation was run.

## E2E user journeys

**BLOCKED locally** — `test/journey-session-titles.spec.ts` uses a journey-owned loopback model and covers long Chinese and English first messages → oversized model output → shorter complete title → persisted title after reload → sidebar CSS and full-title tooltip. A third scenario covers reasoning-only output retaining a safe default. The stub is explicitly enabled only for this journey.

The added journey has been discovered and its metadata checked, but has not yet been executed successfully. The updated GitHub Actions run must establish the Linux full-layer results; no previous-tip CI result is presented as validation of this update.

## Release

Release category: `release:fix` (existing label retained).

User impact: Complete automatic titles without reasoning content or stored truncation ellipses. An oversized result may require one additional naming request.

Compatibility and migration: No data migration or API shape change; existing titles are unchanged.

Closes #314

## Authorization and execution

- Allow once returns a one-use authorization; Allow matching reuses consent only for the exact command, target instance, account, workspace/cwd, Session, Agent and run. No fixed TTL. Revocation, run completion/cancellation, target/account changes and Runner restart prevent reuse. Child Agents receive no inherited direct grant.
- Require a new `run_direct_shell` call confirming the returned scope. Consume authorization before asynchronous dispatch, preserve durable Execution IDs, and block further direct authorization when the Agent has an unknown local execution outcome.

Hash Runner ID, instance, account, target-side workspace/cwd, command, Session, Agent and run into the separate direct permission resource. 372.body:
Session-enabled connectors stayed listed, and the agent received none of their tools, when the MCP server was switched off or could not connect. The catalog already recorded that state. The connector list ignored it.

## Disabled servers stay out of the picker and the agent

A server that is turned off, or that never entered the resolved server table, is reported as `disabled` once a catalog has been applied. `GET /api/connectors` omits those connectors, so the composer, settings, the project form, and the specialist form no longer offer them. Tool injection is unchanged: a disabled source has no available tools, so the agent is not given `mcp__<source>__*` tools even when the session still names the connector. The MCP server settings page still shows the disabled server and its switch, so it can be turned back on. Turning it back on returns the connectors to the picker with the previous selection.

## Connection failures stay visible

An enabled server that fails to connect or to list its tools stays in the connector list. Each of its connectors carries `connectionError`: the server's error text and the time the catalog was checked. The picker shows that text under the connector. The composer control shows a failure count when a selected connector failed. A partial tool mismatch (`degraded`) and a catalog that was never refreshed are left as they were: they are not hidden, and they are not labeled as connection failures.

A direct edit of `extensions_config.json` appears after the next catalog refresh (process start, `POST /api/mcp/sources/reload`, or saving a custom server). That is the same moment the agent sees the change.

## Compatibility

When an applied catalog does not contain a server, source status is `disabled` rather than `unavailable`. The governance broker rejects a call in that case with `MCP server is disabled or not configured: <id>`. Connectors of a disabled server are absent from `GET /api/connectors`.

Related to #325.

## Validation

Recorded on `4c9baed756f8b0ebbb33eaf967197e970e07af53`.

- Typecheck for the web, api, mcp, data-source, schema, and artifact-manager packages, plus `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json`: passed.
- Package tests: web 890/890, data-source 51/51, mcp-sources 28/28, schema 12/12, mcp 1/1, artifact-manager 2/2.
- `services/api`: 1128 passed, 3 failed. The failures are PDF extraction tests and exit with `spawn … ENOENT` because `services/paper/.venv` is not present in this checkout. They do not call the connector list.
- `pnpm docs:check`, `pnpm architecture:check`, and `pnpm ci:selftest` (55/55) passed. The E2E meta check reported 0 errors.

`pnpm ci:ut`, `pnpm ci:st`, and `pnpm ci:e2e` were not run. Those layers provision JiuwenSwarm outside the repository tree, which this environment does not allow. This pull request is a draft until those layers have results.

## E2E user journeys

PASS for the connector journey on `4c9baed756f8b0ebbb33eaf967197e970e07af53`. Local stack, native executor, runner and API on ports 4480 and 4481.

`test/journey-custom-mcp.spec.ts`: 3 passed, 0 failed. Two custom MCP servers are used, one healthy and one that exits during the handshake. Both appear, and only the failing one shows its error. Turning the healthy server off removes its connector from the picker and from the next run's tool list; the settings row and switch remain. Turning it on brings the connector back, still selected.

`journey-plugin-composition`: the connector-panel step passed. A later step expects `todo_create`, which the native executor does not provide. That failure is outside this change.

The mocked `pnpm ci:e2e` layer was not run.

## Release

User impact: connectors whose MCP server is off disappear from the picker and are not offered to the agent. A connector whose enabled server fails to connect stays listed and shows the connection error.

Compatibility and migration: callers that treated "missing from an applied catalog" as `unavailable`, or that expected those connectors to remain in `GET /api/connectors`, need to handle `disabled` and the shorter list. No configuration change is required.

undici, katex, the MCP TypeScript SDK and the gateway's Python `mcp` are all locked inside the affected range of published advisories: undici 8.9.0 (#369), katex 0.16.47 (#370), `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` 1.30.0 (#371) and `mcp` 1.28.1 (CVE-2026-59951). This moves each one past its fix, on the same major line, and leaves every other dependency where it was. No lower copy of any of the four stays in either lockfile.

Fixes #369
Fixes #370
Fixes #371

| Package | Before | After | Advisories |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `undici` (`services/api`, `packages/model`, `packages/data-source`) | 8.9.0 | 8.12.2 | CVE-2026-85024, -85008, -19534, -84961, -84947, -18149, -84890, -84933, -85014, -18540 (fixed in 8.10.2) |
| `katex` (`apps/web`, and the copies inside `rehype-katex` and `micromark-extension-math`) | 0.16.47 | 0.18.10 | CVE-2026-103923 (fixed in 0.18.2) |
| `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` (`services/api`) | 1.30.0 | 1.31.0 | CVE-2026-104850 (fixed in 1.31.0) |
| `mcp` (`services/gateway`) | 1.28.1, range `>=1.0.0` | 1.30.0, range `>=1.30.0,<2` | CVE-2026-59951 (fixed in 1.30.0) |

## undici 8.12.2

The ten advisories in #369 are fixed in 8.10.2, but 8.10.2 is not a good place to stop: 8.12.2 ships fixes for eight further advisories published after it, including a process crash on a TLS 1.2 certificate-changing renegotiation (CVE-2026-87018) and `Agent` dropping function-valued TLS options such as `checkServerIdentity` (CVE-2026-109383). 8.12.2 is the newest 8.x release, so the tree stays on 8.x instead of taking the 7.29.1 or 6.28.1 backports.

The issue names `services/api` and `packages/model`; `packages/data-source` pins the same exact version for the proxy `fetch`, so all three move together and the lock keeps one copy.

## katex 0.18.10, for the whole tree

0.18.10 is the newest release that can be taken as-is. 0.18.11 is deprecated upstream as accidentally published with a breaking change, and 0.19.0 is that change (missing character metrics are reported through `strict`, which changes warnings and strict-mode errors).

Bumping `apps/web` alone would leave 0.16.47 in the lock: `rehype-katex` 7.0.1 and `micromark-extension-math` 3.1.0 (pulled in by `remark-math`) are both at their latest release and still ask for `katex ^0.16`. `rehype-katex` does not have a newer release to move to. A workspace override, next to the existing `ajv` one, puts the whole tree on one katex.

That is also what keeps formulas rendering correctly. KaTeX 0.18.0 prefixed its internal classes (`base` → `katex-base`, `strut` → `katex-strut`, and so on). The stylesheet comes from `apps/web`'s katex, while the markup comes from `rehype-katex`'s copy, so a 0.16 renderer under the 0.18 stylesheet would lose those layout rules. `rehype-katex` only calls `katex.renderToString`, which 0.18 keeps. `apps/web` styles only `.katex-display`, which did not change.

katex now ships its own type declarations and `apps/web` only imports its stylesheet, so the direct `@types/katex` dev dependency is dropped. `@types/katex` 0.16.8 stays in the lock as a declared dependency of `rehype-katex` and `micromark-extension-math`. It contains type declarations only and has no newer release.

## @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.31.0

The package stays `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` 1.x rather than moving to `@modelcontextprotocol/client` 2.x. 1.31.0 rather than 1.32.x on purpose: 1.32.0 also makes the HTTP client transports refuse cross-origin redirects, a behaviour change for custom MCP servers that the advisory does not need. That belongs in its own change.

1.31.0 binds stored OAuth credentials to the authorization server that issued them by stamping an `issuer` field on what it passes to `saveTokens()` and `saveClientInformation()`. The custom-MCP `OAuthClientProvider` in `services/api/src/mcp/oauth.ts` stores both objects whole, so the stamp is persisted without a code change, and the provider still compiles against the new types. Credentials saved by 1.30.0 have no stamp. The SDK still uses them, logs one warning, and stamps them on the first successful refresh, so existing sign-ins keep working without a new login.

## Gateway mcp >=1.30.0,<2

The gateway declared `mcp>=1.0.0` and locked 1.28.1. CVE-2026-59951 is about unbounded session accumulation in the Streamable HTTP server transport. The advisory says stdio is not affected, and the bundled FastMCP servers keep running with `transport="stdio"`, so this is a version floor, not a transport change. The floor makes sure neither the lock nor a fresh resolve can install an affected version. The range stops below 2: 2.x is a separate major line. Relocking moves only `mcp`, to 1.30.0, the newest 1.x release; its dependencies resolve as before. There is no GitHub issue for this one, so nothing is closed for it.

## Third-party notice

The notice tracks the shipped versions: undici, katex, and katex's `commander` dependency (8.3.0 → 15.0.0) are updated. Their copyright lines are unchanged.

## Validation

Tested commit: `397ade685780d51060802b528531c9934a6947a1`, all three layers run locally on Linux x64 with the bubblewrap sandbox available.

| Layer | Command | planned | executed | passed | failed | skipped |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| UT | `pnpm ci:ut` | 3873 | 3873 | 3873 | 0 | 0 |
| ST | `pnpm ci:st` | 3 | 3 | 3 | 0 | 0 |
| E2E (mocked browser subset) | `pnpm ci:e2e` | 75 | 75 | 75 | 0 | 0 |

The UT layer includes the suites closest to each bump: `apps/web` Markdown rendering (16, inline, display, `\(…\)` / `\[…\]` math and shell `$` staying text), custom-MCP OAuth (7) and the MCP node client (14) in `services/api`, the evolution LLM proxy that uses undici `fetch` (12), `packages/model` (48), `packages/data-source` (51), and the gateway's Python tests (28) on `mcp` 1.30.0. `pnpm build` and `pnpm typecheck` also pass.

Targeted checks on the same tree:

- **OAuth credentials saved before this change.** A one-off script signed in to the repository's OAuth MCP fixture, removed `issuer` from the encrypted credential store to reproduce what 1.30.0 saved, reloaded the store, expired the access token and listed tools. The refresh token was accepted (one refresh against the fixture's token endpoint), tools were listed, and the stored tokens and client information carried `issuer` afterwards. Checked with dynamic client registration and with a pre-registered client. The SDK logs one warning on that first refresh.
- **Gateway over stdio.** Each bundled server (UniProt, biomed, LLM wiki) was started as a subprocess and driven by the `mcp` 1.30.0 stdio client: all three initialize (protocol 2025-11-25) and list their tools (3, 33 and 3).
- **Formula rendering, visually.** Sample Markdown with inline math, `$$` and `\[…\]` display blocks, `aligned`, `pmatrix`, `\sum` with limits, `\left(…\right)` and one malformed formula was rendered through the real `MarkdownRenderer` (remark-math + rehype-katex) and opened with the stylesheet from `pnpm build` in the pinned Chromium. All KaTeX fonts loaded with no failed requests, the formulas laid out correctly, the malformed one fell back to the red source text as before, and `$5` prices stayed text.
- **Lockfiles.** `pnpm-lock.yaml` resolves `undici@8.12.2`, `katex@0.18.10` (one copy) and `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk@1.31.0`, and holds no `@modelcontextprotocol/client`. `services/gateway/uv.lock` resolves `mcp` 1.30.0.

## E2E user journeys

**PASS** on `397ade685780d51060802b528531c9934a6947a1`. Browser journeys in the pinned Playwright Chromium against an isolated local stack (JiuwenSwarm executor, mocked model): 75 discovered, 75 passed, 0 failed, 0 blocked, 0 skipped (research fixture 20, standard 49, literature 6). Command: `pnpm ci:e2e`.

- **MCP SDK.** `journey-mcp-oauth`, *Authorize MCP, inspect tools and recover from denied consent*: the user configures an OAuth-protected custom MCP server and signs in through the browser consent flow → the PKCE callback connects and lists its tools, the Inspector runs a tool without a separately supplied token, an expired access token is refreshed with exactly one `refresh_token` request, a denied re-authorization shows an error, the next consent restores the connection, and clearing the local authorization requires a new sign-in → PASS. `journey-custom-mcp` (2: the Custom MCP and Inspector journey, and an agent using selected custom MCP servers across runs), `journey-mcp-secret-edit` (2) and `swarm-specialist-mcp-mocked` (1) also PASS.
- **undici.** Every journey that runs an agent turn sends its model requests through `packages/model`'s undici client to the mock model.
- **katex: coverage gap.** No E2E journey renders math, so formula rendering in the browser is not covered by this layer. It is covered here by the UT rendering tests and the visual check above; adding a journey whose mocked answer contains math would close the gap.
- **Gateway mcp.** No mocked journey asserts on the bundled Python MCP servers (the literature journeys use an offline MCP fixture), so they are covered by the gateway UT suite and the stdio check above.

## Release
Release category: release:dependency
User impact: none intended. Math in Markdown renders through KaTeX 0.18.10 instead of 0.16.47; custom MCP OAuth sign-ins and the bundled stdio MCP servers behave as before.
Compatibility and migration: none. Custom-MCP OAuth credentials saved before this change keep working and are bound to their authorization server on their first refresh.

Fixes #30

Neither README mentions `ScienceDiscovery run`, so a researcher who wants to script or batch runs has no way to learn the command-line client exists. The deployment guides show only `serve`, and the CLI reference never names the flag a non-interactive run needs. This PR adds a short command-line section to both READMEs, a command list to both deployment guides, and names `--auto-approve` in the CLI reference.

## README: command line (English and Chinese)

- A new **Command line** section after the capability table shows three runnable commands: a terminal run, a piped run filtered with `jq`, and an answer written to a file. One paragraph states the TTY versus pipe difference, that a non-interactive run must pass `--auto-approve`, and what that option allows: it approves the session's tool actions, except direct host execution after a sandbox failure, which always needs explicit consent.
- The examples differ from the issue's sketch on purpose. On current `main`, `run "…" > answer.md` does not produce a clean file: a redirected stdout is not a TTY, so `run` defaults to JSONL and refuses to start without `--auto-approve`, which leaves one JSON error line in the file and exits 1 (scenario 6 below). The file example therefore uses `--auto-approve --output text`.
- The capability table gets a **Scripted and batch runs** row, and the Documentation table's Reference row links the CLI reference.
- Commands, defaults and behaviour come from `services/launcher/src/cli-options.ts` and `services/launcher/src/run.ts` at `cf6c71c2`.

## Deployment guides and CLI reference

- The guide this issue names, `docs/en/how-to/deployment.md`, now lives at `docs/en/getting-started/deployment.md`. Both language versions now list `serve`, `run`, `extract`, `version` and `help` in matching tables, with a pointer to the CLI reference and the source-mode entry point.
- The CLI reference exists in both languages, so the README links to it. It now says `--auto-approve` (or `--approval always_allow`) instead of "the appropriate automatic-approval option", and shows the text-to-file example.

## Relationship with #219, #27 and #318

#219 removed an earlier README command-line section to simplify the homepage. This issue's acceptance criteria ask for the CLI in both READMEs, so it returns as one short section (three commands, one paragraph) that leaves the option list to the CLI reference. #27 (README security warning) is a separate pull request; the two change different lines and `git merge-tree` merges them cleanly in either order. They also merge cleanly with open #318.

## Validation

- `pnpm docs:check`: markdownlint 126 files, 0 issues; link check passed for 126 Markdown files.
- `git diff --check`: clean.
- The added docs-site links (CLI reference, English and Chinese) return HTTP 200.
- The UT, ST and mocked E2E layers were not run locally. This diff changes only Markdown (READMEs, deployment guides, CLI reference), with no code, test or build input; this PR's CI runs them.

## E2E user journeys

**PASS.** This was a CLI journey over the commands the README documents. Tested code: `cf6c71c2`; this PR's head differs from it only in Markdown. The journey ran when the head was `809c6fcf`. The later commit `3fe05546` only rewords two sentences after review and leaves the commands unchanged. It ran against an isolated local stack built from source, with the sandbox runner and control API on loopback, the native agent loop, and scientific environments off. A real model served it (`deepseek-flash` through an OpenAI-compatible endpoint). The client was `node services/launcher/dist/main.js run`, the source-mode equivalent of `./ScienceDiscovery run`. It ran from the directory that holds `./.sciencediscovery-data`, with `--port` matching `serve`, as the README says.

| # | Scenario | Expected | Actual |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `help` | Lists the five commands in the new deployment tables | PASS: 5 of 5 |
| 2 | Terminal example, stdout on a pseudo-terminal | Text mode, interactive, answer on stdout, progress on stderr | PASS: exit 0, `interactive=true approval=ask_for_dangerous`, answer on the terminal, `[run]` lines only on stderr |
| 3 | Pipe example: `--auto-approve` piped through the README's `jq` filter | JSONL only; the filter prints the final answer | PASS: exit 0, 545 lines, 0 non-JSON lines, `result.status=completed`, 3,033-byte answer |
| 4 | `--auto-approve --output text "…" > answer.md` | The file holds only the answer | PASS: exit 0, 2,060-byte answer, 0 status or JSON lines in the file, `[run] completed` on stderr |
| 5 | Pipe without `--auto-approve` | Refused with a JSON error | PASS: exit 1, `{"type":"error",…,"code":"NON_INTERACTIVE_NO_AUTO_APPROVE"}` |
| 6 | The issue's `run "…" > answer.md` without flags | Shows why the README differs | Exit 1; the file holds the JSON refusal, not an answer |

Totals: 6 passed, 0 failed, 0 blocked, 0 skipped.

How long a run takes depends on what the agent decides to do. The same pipe example finished in 8 s on one run and in 478 s on another, where the agent chose to research first. The README promises no timing. In an earlier attempt at scenario 2, the agent asked to write a file. The permission menu appeared in the terminal, and answering `1` let the run complete.

One defect showed up that this PR does not change. When an interactive run waits about five minutes at a permission prompt, the client prints `[run] failed: terminated` and stays at `Choose [1-3]:`, while the run is still `blocked` on the server. The likely cause is that the run event stream sends nothing while blocked, so the client's idle body timeout closes it.

## Release

Release category: `release:docs`
User impact: Readers of either README learn that the command-line client exists, how to script it, and why a non-interactive run needs `--auto-approve`. Both deployment guides now list every launcher command.
Compatibility and migration: none.

Fixes #29

Most of this issue is already on `main`. `scripts/start-stack.sh` collects every missing host tool before it exits, prints what is missing with a concrete remedy for node, pnpm, python3, uv and curl, and the Node gate reports the version it found. Two gaps remained, both on the source-mode path:

1. **The report's documentation link was dead.** Its footer pointed to `docs/en/how-to/deployment.md#local-mode-host-processes`, which no longer exists. The README requirements row it also points to did not list curl or Bubblewrap.
2. **Nothing told a source-mode user how to get bubblewrap or sandbox-exec.** Startup deliberately stopped checking for them; the Runner probes for them itself. When the executable is missing, the Runner's readiness report carried only the raw `spawn bwrap ENOENT`. It wrote the problem only to its log file, so the terminal said nothing. The Settings "Execution readiness" card showed `spawn bwrap ENOENT` with no remedy.

## Runner: say how to install a missing sandbox executable

- `missingSandboxExecutableMessage` in `@sciencediscovery/sandbox-capability` returns three lines:
  - **Bubblewrap:** the package is named bubblewrap and provides the bwrap executable. It gives the apt and dnf commands and links `deployment.md#linux-reports-missing-bwrap`.
  - **sandbox-exec:** it ships with macOS and is not installed separately, so a missing one means a parent sandbox or a wrong `SCIENCE_AGENT_SEATBELT_PATH`. It links `#macos-reports-seatbelt-is-unavailable`.
- `RunnerReadiness` uses this message as `detail` when the probe cannot spawn the executable (`ENOENT`/`EACCES`). Other probe outcomes keep their current detail.
- At startup, the Runner also prints this message to the terminal that started it, so `start-stack.sh` users see it next to the rest of the startup output. The capability report and the Settings card show the same text.
- Startup still does not block on a missing sandbox; the Runner reports it instead. The `start-stack.sh` comment now says so explicitly.

## start-stack: link the current guide

- The footer now points to `docs/en/getting-started/deployment.md#local-source-mode-linux--macos`. That section lists Node.js, pnpm, python3, uv, Git, curl and the sandbox per platform.
- The README "Local source mode" requirements row (English and Chinese) adds curl and Bubblewrap on Linux, so both printed links cover every dependency the report can name.
- The same stale `#local-mode-host-processes` anchor is replaced in `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `services/adapter/README.md`, and an old `how-to` path in a `package-binary-release.sh` comment.

The issue's open question asked whether commands should be inline or behind a doc link. This keeps the shape already on `main`: one remedy inline and one shared link, and each entry stays at three lines or fewer.

## Validation

Tested commit: `cb3853f5`, which is this PR's head.

- Runner unit tests (`services/runner/src/readiness.test.ts`): 3 passed, including the new case. It asserts both the bubblewrap and the sandbox-exec text and the three-line limit.
- UT layer (`pnpm ci:ut`): PASS, 3,874 planned, 3,874 executed, 3,874 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.
- ST layer (`pnpm ci:st`): PASS, 3 planned, 3 passed.
- Mocked E2E layer (`pnpm ci:e2e`): PASS, 75 planned, 75 executed, 75 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped. This is the browser subset; this PR's own user journey is below.
- `pnpm docs:check`: markdownlint 126 files, 0 issues; link check passed for 126 Markdown files.
- `git diff --check`: clean.

## E2E user journeys

**PASS.** Tested commit: `cb3853f5`. The new driver is `test/api/source-start-dependency-journey.mjs` (run with `node test/api/source-start-dependency-journey.mjs` after `pnpm build`). It goes through the real `scripts/start-stack.sh`, the built Runner and the control API on loopback. It needs no model and no network.

| # | Scenario | Expected | Actual |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `start-stack.sh --mode local` on a host with none of node, pnpm, python3, uv, curl | One report listing all five, each with a remedy line, then exit before anything starts | PASS: exit 1; `5 host dependency problem(s)`; every entry has an indented remedy; 21 lines in total |
| 2 | Same, with only Node v20.11.0 installed | The version found and how to upgrade | PASS: `Node.js 22.19+ is required; found v20.11.0.` then `Upgrade it, …` |
| 3 | Follow the printed links | Each `path#anchor` matches a heading that covers those dependencies | PASS: `README.md#requirements` and `deployment.md#local-source-mode-linux--macos` resolve; the README row and the guide section name every dependency; the Runner's two anchors resolve too |
| 4 | Tools present, no `bwrap` on PATH, start the Runner as `start-stack.sh` does | The terminal names the package, the binary and the install command | PASS: three lines on stderr (shown below); `/execution-capability` reports `dependency-unavailable` with the same text |
| 5 | The readiness the Web UI reads (`/api/runners/local/execution-capability`) | The same remedy reaches the Settings card | PASS: `connected: true`, `ready: false`, the detail carries the remedy and the anchor |

Totals: 5 passed, 0 failed, 0 blocked, 0 skipped.

Terminal output of the Runner in scenario 4:

```text
bubblewrap is not available: "bwrap" could not be started (spawn bwrap ENOENT).
Install the bubblewrap package, which provides the bwrap executable: sudo apt-get install -y bubblewrap (Debian/Ubuntu) or sudo dnf install -y bubblewrap (Fedora/RHEL/openEuler). Then recheck the Runner.
Details: docs/en/getting-started/deployment.md#linux-reports-missing-bwrap
```

The Settings → Local Runner "Execution readiness" card on the same kind of stack, in a headless browser. Before this change, the card's message line read only `spawn bwrap ENOENT`:

![Execution readiness card naming the bubblewrap package, the bwrap executable, the install commands and the troubleshooting section](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3d190210-514b-4f56-8afb-f03c23ab5340)

The macOS `sandbox-exec` path could not run on this Linux host. Its message is covered by the unit test, which probes a missing `sandbox-exec` path on Linux and gets the same spawn failure.

User impact: A source-mode start that fails on host tools now links a guide section that exists. A host without bubblewrap, or with a broken sandbox-exec, is told in the terminal and in Settings what to install or check.

380.body:
Fixes #26

At `cf6c71c2`, the quick start already has a concrete first task, and all 17 bundled Skills are named in the built-in capabilities reference (the issue counted 18; `skills/` has changed since). Two things were still missing: a sample file shipped in the repository that a tutorial uses directly, and a learning path that continues after the quick start. The domain cases link back to the quick start instead of onward, and they take one to two hours. This PR adds a synthetic sample CSV and five short lessons in English and Chinese, and chains the quick start and the lessons together.

## Where the lessons live

`docs/*/tutorial/` was removed when the docs were restructured. The getting-started section now covers "install, configure and complete a first task". The lessons extend it with descriptive slugs and no numeric prefixes, as #117 proposed. Acceptance criterion 1 is therefore met as "the getting-started learning path has more than one lesson, and each links to the next". The order:

1. `quick-start.md` (existing). Its "Where to go next" now starts with the next lesson.
2. `analyze-a-dataset.md`: upload the shipped CSV, approve the first code execution, and find a box plot and a report among the Artifacts.
3. `literature-search-and-report.md`: turn on the PubMed and Europe PMC connectors and use `literature-searcher`, `evidence-extractor` and `report-writer` to get a cited evidence summary.
4. `use-and-write-skills.md`: run the bundled `computation-reviewer` on the previous report, create a Skill with `skill-creator`, review and publish the draft, turn its library on, and run it.
5. `connect-a-tool.md`: add a public MCP server (DeepWiki, no account or key), test it, enable it for one Session, and use it.
6. `trace-a-result.md`: follow the figure to its command, exit code and package versions, act on the Reviewer's findings to get version 2 of the report, open both versions from the version selector to check that only links were added, and revoke the grant from lesson 2.

Every lesson gives the time, what you need, the input, the exact prompt, the Skills and connectors it uses, "What you should see", a checklist, and a link to the next lesson. Results are described by their shape, not by fixed text or numbers. The last lesson points to the domain guides. Both language indexes list the path in order.

## The sample file

`docs/examples/plant-growth.csv` is 45 rows and about 1 KB: plant id, one of three fertilizer treatments, daily light hours and dry mass. The values are synthetic, generated for these tutorials, and describe no real plants. They are distributed under the repository's Apache-2.0 license, as `docs/examples/README.md` states. Binary users have no checkout, so the lesson gives a `curl -LO` command for the raw file on `main`. Light hours are deliberately not balanced across treatments, so the dataset lesson asks the Agent to check that confounder.

## Choices on the issue's open questions

- **Flagship case:** CSV analysis on the shipped file, because it is the one that can run end to end without external services. The literature case comes next and links to the longer domain guide instead of repeating it.
- **Installation path:** the lessons start after the quick start, so they work for the binary, source and Docker alike; the only path-specific step is how to get the sample file.
- **Screenshots:** none were added. The lessons name UI labels instead, checked against both locales in `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts`.
- **#117:** this covers its dataset and literature lessons. Model setup stays in the quick start, so #117 is left open for maintainers to decide.

## Validation

- `pnpm docs:check`: markdownlint 137 files, 0 issues; link check passed for 137 Markdown files.
- `git diff --check`: clean. The English and Chinese pages have the same headings, code blocks and links.
- The UT, ST and mocked E2E layers were not run locally. The diff is Markdown plus one CSV, and no code, test or build input changes; this PR's CI runs them.

## E2E user journeys

**PASS.** Each lesson was followed against a real local stack started with `scripts/start-stack.sh --mode local` on `cf6c71c2`; this PR's head differs from it only in docs. The stack used the default JiuwenSwarm backend, a managed Python environment (pandas 2.2, SciPy 1.14, Matplotlib 3.9) that installed itself in about a minute, and a real model (`deepseek-flash` through an OpenAI-compatible endpoint). A script drove the public HTTP API the web UI uses. It created Projects and Sessions, uploaded the shipped CSV through the workspace upload endpoint, sent each lesson's exact English prompt, answered the permission requests, and waited for the terminal state.

| Lesson | Runs | Outcome | Permission requests |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Analyze a dataset | 3, all completed (241 s, 178 s, 130 s) | Code ran in the managed Python environment; `growth-report.md` and `treatment-boxplot.png` registered as Artifacts next to the uploaded CSV | 1 "Run local code" |
| Literature search and report | 1, completed (about 15 min) | `biochar-yield-summary.md` with its source list and evidence table; 10 studies, each reference with a DOI and a link | 6 connector searches (PubMed, Europe PMC) and 1 code |
| Use and write Skills, step 1 | 1, completed (392 s) | `computation-reviewer` loaded; `computation-check.md` registered | none (the Session's grant from the earlier lesson applied) |
| Use and write Skills, steps 2–3 | 1, completed (380 s) | `skill-creator` produced a three-file draft, which was published to Project Skills through the endpoint the **Publish Skill** button calls | none |

This PR exports the existing main-agent/independent-worker Issue-to-PR workflow as opt-in contributor tooling. Scheduling decisions stay with the main agent rather than a script-driven queue controller. It does not modify ScienceDiscovery's research agent runtime, CI policy, repository settings or the operator's running pipeline.

## Scope

- Add `.agents/skills/repo-issue-pipeline` with the coordination policy, worker contract and operational guidance: claim before admission, reproduce before implementation, full accepted-scope delivery, original-thread resume, change-driven discussion/CI/conflict maintenance, independent main-agent review and explicit human/authority boundaries.
- Export a portable one-turn Codex SDK transport with an optional executable override instead of a machine-specific CLI path. Requests explicitly acknowledge full host access; per-session locks prevent concurrent hosts, saved threads resume in their original worktree, and private session/events/final/failure records survive handoff. An incomplete or failed stream cannot be reported as successful.
- Add 16 hermetic tagged tests to the existing `scripts/*.test.mjs` discovery path, without introducing a second CI definition or requiring model tokens.
- Add English/Chinese developer overviews and contributor navigation, plus a setup guide covering private ledgers, configurable repositories/concurrency/inspection interval, resource and cost limits, continuation, systemd examples, recovery and raw-log sensitivity.

## Deliberate boundaries

This is an opt-in developer tool, not a product background service or automatic installer. No real task ledger, account, credentials, logs, host-specific services or legacy migration code are included. Cloning/installing the skill starts nothing. Workers have explicitly authorized full host access, so this must not be attached to untrusted PR/webhook execution. Worktrees are not sandboxes. Raw private logs can contain tool secrets and must not become public CI artifacts.

Periodic wake-up is documented but must be configured and verified on the target host. Completion-event wake-ups and a cross-platform daemon installer are not implemented. The main agent, not the host script, enforces the task-pool cap and repository authority. Successful SDK turns and green CI do not establish full Issue acceptance. Merging/enqueueing/releases/settings/secrets/gate changes and paid real-model tests need separate matching authority.
